VIRTUAL TERMINAL FOUNDATION CONTRACT — RUSSL 0.3.0

1. TERMINAL SURFACE
The shell owns the command catalogue, editable sequence composer, ordered
execution, typed result envelopes, command provenance, and snapshot ledger.
Only registered commands are executable. Uploaded candidate documents and
imported histories stay inert. Every implemented operation has a visible entry.

2. MATHEMATICAL ENGINE
src/engine.js is a dependency-free numerical module with a browser global and
CommonJS exports. Field labels encode polynomial coefficients in base p.
Prime GF3 and GF4/GF8/GF9/GF16 have declared field profiles. Integer values
are labels, not ordinary modular integers for extension-field multiplication.
Small-field amplitudes are ordinary complex values. The normalized positive
trace-character Fourier transform, shift, phase, and Frobenius label permutation
are the initial executable candidate. Arithmetic and mathematical checks are
tested independently of the UI. Custom vectors must already be normalized.

src/refined-field.js adds odd-characteristic quadratic characters, symmetric
displacement, point reflection, and normalized pure-state Wigner evaluation.
GF3 and GF9 supply registered odd-characteristic profiles. The
specific half-phase and reflection/Wigner formulas reject characteristic two.
The displacement convention is chi(-xi*zeta/2) Z(zeta) X(xi); reflection at
(q0,p0) maps input label y=2*q0-x to output x with character chi(p0*(x-y)).
W(q0,p0)=<psi|R(q0,p0)|psi>/q has position rows and momentum columns. Its
momentum marginal uses the engine's negative-sign Fourier transform. Returns
include reality, normalization, position/momentum marginal and purity checks,
with mana defined as log2(sum(abs(W))). Raw numerical values are not clipped.

The 2x2 symplectic command is a finite-field label calculation in any registered
field: M^T Omega M=det(M) Omega, and preservation requires det(M)=1 in that
field. It reports the determinant and mapped labels; no general metaplectic
amplitude operator is inferred from the matrix.

src/refined-scalar.js is a separate ordinary real/complex/integer domain.
Clebsch–Gordan coefficients use SU(2), the Condon–Shortley phase convention,
selection rules, bounded integer/half-integer spins, and exact rational squared
coefficients. Arithmetic delta uses integer lifts modulo p^2 with output modulo
p, exact division before reduction, and primes 2..97. It is not an additive
ordinary derivative and is not an operation on the extension-field labels.

The scalar Cayley demonstration solves the corrected forward equation
(I+i*dt*H/(2*hbar))*psi_next=(I-i*dt*H/(2*hbar))*psi_now for a declared finite
Hermitian complex H. It returns the calculated state, solve and norm residuals,
and precision status without renormalization. This bounded inspect-only
calculation does not alter the active finite-field state. Its rational time
step approximates the exponential; no exact long-time phase or finite-field
positive-norm claim is made.

3. RUSSL ADAPTER
The original word workbench is a sandboxed local iframe. The derivative only
adds src/workbench-bridge.js to its outer HTML, and a relay to its existing
research iframe. Its original adapter supplies bounded snapshots and exact
replay. Source-window identity, method whitelist, identifiers, data shape, and
UTF-8 byte limits govern each request. Parent and child cannot access each
other's DOM or storage. No native helper or external API is called.
See workbench-adapter.txt for message schemas and source-witness scope.

4. RESULT AND EVIDENCE CONTRACTS
Return envelopes include id, command, success, summary, declared profile,
elapsed browser wall time, and structured details. They are locally measured
calculations, not native throughput or device instruction counts.
RUSSL-research-record/1 contains kind, label, capture time, and snapshot payload.
SHA-256 uses canonical JSON with recursively sorted object keys and array order
preserved. The hash sits outside the data it covers. RUSSL-virtual-session/1
packages snapshots, records, and optional recent returns/history. Integrity is
separate from mathematical validity and source authorship. Imported records
remain inert. GF80 replay rechecks bounded units and evolved pixels through
the existing workbench; small-field Restore validates values and audits state.
Small-field Restore runs through the serialized ledger.restore command path,
including hash checking, visible rejection, a structured return, and provenance.
Session exports use version 0.3.0 in the existing schema; the importer also
accepts versions 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 when their field and operator conventions
validate. Historical record data and covered hashes are retained unchanged;
imported commands never execute.

5. EQUATION AUDIT AND REPORT INTEGRATION
The supplied audit narrative is preserved unchanged as a source. The Equation
audit view, equation-audit.json, and docs/Equation_Audit.txt connect displayed
formulas and source line numbers with verified, refined, rejected or unresolved
dispositions, declared domains, references and available commands. Candidate
equation numbers are aliases from that report, not primary-paper equation
numbers and not proof that the unavailable 500-equation suite was inspected.

eq.list optionally filters a disposition; eq.show inspects an entry; eq.export
downloads the register. eq.verify runs bounded runtime smoke checks for
implemented definitions. The full automated test suite is a separate check.
Reference-only rejected or unresolved formulas have no executable equation
adapter. In particular, the reported Klein transmission, unspecified modular
partial waves, and conflicting automaton normalizations are not promoted into
physical solvers. Detailed scalar and relativity audits retain counterexamples
and the assumptions required for qualified replacements.

Tests exercise production numerical and command/record code in local fixtures.
Browser rendering, live preview and live iframe behavior remain unverified in
this environment; source tests do not certify those interactions.

6. IMAGE EQUATIONS AND GFM REAPPLICATION
image-equations.json preserves the visible equations of the three supplied
images, their source-byte identities, qualified domains, primary references and
available model families. docs/Image_Equation_Audit.txt records the independent
assessment. Source images remain reference data, with visible attribution and
original rights retained. Formula acceptance applies to the stated ordinary
domain; it does not certify an unrelated field analogue.

The new view accounts for all 20 prior report entries and three image entries.
An applicability manifest names each entry's operator-conjugation, sampled
profile, basis-covariance, retained-metadata or reference-only route. Missing
adapters and rejected/unresolved expressions remain visible. A register entry
does not acquire an execution adapter from its title or source equation number.

The trace-character F is complex and unitary, with one row/column per field
label. Reapplication is an explicit finite basis contract:
  vector y=F*v, then v_returned=F^dagger*y;
  operator A_GFM=F*A*F^dagger, then A_returned=F^dagger*A_GFM*F.
Matrix/vector dimension must match the declared field order. Returned operator
entries remain complex values. Similarity preserves the spectrum and, for a
unitary input operator, unitarity. It does not convert scalar coefficients to
field labels. Checks report numerical round-trip and covariance residuals.

model.pendulum <g> <length> <max-angle-rad> samples ordinary restoring
acceleration -(g/length)*sin(theta) on a declared angle grid. It prepares the
normalized Fourier signal in the active field-sized amplitude interface and
retains the original scale and sample-coordinate metadata in its result.
The accompanying small-angle frequency and period are ordinary mechanical
references. This is a finite signal representation, not a time integrator
or a predicted quantum wavefunction.

model.rotate <axis> <degrees> requires the dimension-three GF3 profile. The
ordinary input R is an active, right-handed axis rotation of column vectors;
degrees are converted to radians. Input and operator are changed together:
the transformed operator F3*R*F3^dagger acts on F3*psi, and the result returns
through F3^dagger. The final active output equals R*psi in its original basis,
with orthogonality, determinant and covariance/recovery checks. The image's
theta=232.75 degrees keeps this ordinary-domain interpretation.

model.zeta <s> accepts real integer s=2..8. Its sampled ordinary Mellin kernel
is normalized into a Fourier signal, with scale and sample bounds retained.
Any quadrature/cutoff comparison is a bounded numerical reference. The source
zeta(s)*Gamma(s) improper integral requires Re(s)>1, and the transformed finite
profile is not a field-valued zeta/Gamma or an improper-integral identity.

model.oscillator <q> <v> <kappa> <h> [steps] inspects exact odd-field velocity
Verlet on dimensionless field coordinates. Its half-step requires 2 invertible.
Reversal and determinant are algebraic checks; no positive energy, physical
seconds, square-root frequency or sinusoidal field function is inferred.
model.fieldrotate <axis> <t|infinity> <X> <Y> <Z> inspects an exact odd-field
quadratic-form rotation. Finite t uses c=(1-t^2)/(1+t^2), s=2t/(1+t^2), and rejects
1+t^2=0. The separate infinity case gives c=-1,s=0. The field matrix has
R^T*R=I and determinant one; its quadratic form is not a positive Euclidean
norm. These inspectors leave the active complex amplitude state unchanged.

model.reapply <stored-id|all> routes entries through their declared adapters or
returns a reference-only disposition. The all route builds full 20+3 coverage
and a GF9 sampled-signal displacement/reflection demonstration. model.verify
checks the new bounded contracts; model.export preserves a reapplication packet.
Examples insert for review and require explicit execution. Stored source text
and old command provenance remain inert.

No identity-preserving ring homomorphism R -> F_p exists: p=0 in F_p, while
1=p*(1/p) in R. Exact finite-field models therefore require separately chosen
algebraic definitions. Integer/rational transport excludes denominators that
vanish in the field. Real sine/cosine/exponential values, arbitrary real
constants, derivatives and continuum integrals cannot be blindly reduced
modulo p. Round-trip checks certify finite representation recovery, not these
missing constructions or any new physical interpretation.

7. EXTENSION POINTS
Add a model by defining its domain, exact label/state representation, operators,
inverse, precision policy, reference equations, and falsifiable checks first.
Register commands only when their execution adapter exists. A future native
SpinDoctor connector should declare service/version, backend availability,
authentication boundaries, accepted input schema, job lifecycle, cancellation
semantics, response accounting, and independent result verification. No native
connector is assumed to be active in this browser-only foundation.

GF80 and small complex-state domains must retain their names and codecs. A
mapping between them needs an explicit contract stating retained/discarded
information. Never reinterpret Pixel160 payloads as arbitrary probability
amplitudes or identify a 5D address domain with a native quantum Hilbert space.

8. FUTURE RESEARCH
Candidate extensions include even-characteristic phase-space constructions,
mixed-state Wigner functions, general metaplectic amplitude operators, affine
striations and MUBs, coding-transform modules, and p-adic models. Each requires
its own definitions, state representation, domain restrictions, and independent
checks before execution. The finite complex and exact field models in release
0.3 do not establish these missing sectors or a universal physical theory.

RELEASE 0.4 HORIZON FOUNDATION

RELEASE 0.4
The Aperture & aggie view integrates the supplied black-hole PDF, three metric/
aperture diagrams, tensor-map screenshot and the preserved user write-up.
The register contains 49 findings: all 23 numbered PDF equations, 22 image
formula groups and four narrative qualifications. Each source expression,
audited correction, domain and applicability is retained separately.

Standard Schwarzschild, Reissner–Nordström, Kerr and Kerr–Newman references
include horizons, exterior metrics, thermodynamics, Smarr and charged mass
identities. GFM encodes selected exterior scalar samples and hypothetical
aperture/passage samples with the grid, units and original L2 scale retained.
It does not prove metric equivalence or solve a formation/perturbation system.

The proposed gaseous aperture and aggie cover remain explicitly hypothetical.
With identical permitted exterior observations, posterior probabilities equal
the priors; balanced classification cannot exceed 50%. An optional toy passage
test distinguishes different assumed passage bits and therefore changes the
all-tests-indistinguishable premise. Extreme spin is not timeless matter;
the proposed electromagnetic zap has no supplied interaction law.

Open Aperture & aggie, adjust the case and select Apply & compare. Load GFM
signal recomputes the audited report, prepares the GF9 exterior signal followed
by D(3,4) and R(3,4), and adds a ledger record. Existing ledger records remain.
Read docs/Horizon_Simulation_Specification.txt and docs/Horizon_Equation_Audit.txt.
Import examples/Horizon-Simulation-session.json through Evidence & ledger to
reload the saved case, three state records and complete numeric report.
Import replaces the active session after validating its integrity and domains.
